title: Reading Patchbook — compact heuristics, KV friction, and quick experiment ideas
content:
Quick context: this is a messy dump from a week of reading papers + a couple of talk recordings (ICLR / internal watch party). The goal is a short list of concrete experiments and a few heuristics we might fold into the inference playground. Not polished — notes to self and for Maya / Ravi to skim.

High-level takeaways (short):
- Many recent papers push small, low-compute changes that give outsized improvements on long-context throughput (KV compression, chunked attention kernels, prefix caching heuristics). Worth exploring cheaply.
- The main engineering friction is not algorithmic complexity but integration surface: cache invalidation, shard placement, and compatibility with existing batching code.
- Evaluation: need short, targeted probes (5–10 prompts) to catch quality regressions rather than full-scale evals for early-stage experiments.

Papers / vids I pulled: (quick one-liners)
- "Locality-aware KV-folding" (arXiv 2601.01234) — compresses contiguous KV regions with low-rank projection; nice theory, simple kernel, but sensitive to distributional shift when queries jump topics quickly.
- "Chunk-attn with overlap windows" — implementation notes: overlap window size is a knob that trades memory for per-step latency; good for long single-stream sessions.
- "Prefix fingerprinting for cache reuse" (talk) — hashing prefixes to reuse cache entries across paraphrased prompts; promising for RAG-heavy workloads.

Concrete small experiments (cheap / 1–3 days):
1) Lightweight KV downprojection: implement a simple random-projection-based downsample of keys/values applied post-attention softmax. Measure throughput on a 4k and 16k synthetic session mix. Metrics: tokens/sec, tail latency (95/99), and delta perplexity on small probe set (10 prompts).
- Why: low engineering upfront, can run as a quick ablation to see sensitivity.
- Risk: quality regressions on QA-style jumps. Keep alpha parameter tunable.

2) Overlap-chunk kernel prototype: modify a local attention kernel to support 2x overlap and variable chunk sizes. Use our microbench harness to sweep chunk size and overlap. Focus on latency vs memory tradeoff for streaming responses.
- Why: realistic for chat use-cases where context grows and we want graceful per-token latency.

3) Prefix fingerprint cache toy: build a tiny wrapper that computes a 128-bit fingerprint over last N tokens and reuses an existing KV cache if Hamming distance < threshold. Run on logged session traces (anonymized) to get hit rate and false-positive quality regressions.
- Data: ask SRE for a 1-hour trace sample from hosted API (non-sensitive).

Notes on evaluation design (keep small & fast):
- Probe set: 12 prompts across modalities — multi-turn dialogue, factual QA, code completion. Short, human-inspected gold. We report both token-level log-prob deltas and qualitative sample checks (2 reviewers).
- Do not push to company-wide eval until ablation on probes looks robust. Small false negatives are OK early.

Integration & ops points to think about:
- Cache invalidation: how do we force eviction when a long-term session changes topic? Add cheap topic-change detector (cosine on last k-token embedding) and evict fingerprint hits if delta > threshold.
- Batching interaction: downprojection reduces per-token compute but may increase variance in runtimes; need to measure tail impact in our batching simulator.
- Telemetry: add a micro-metric for "cache-fingerprint-hit-quality" (sampled cohort) — store a small sample of prompts and responses when reuse happens to flag regressions.

Open questions / things I couldn't find: 
- Stability of prefix fingerprints under paraphrase. Papers mention some robustness but no firm numbers; need a small paraphrase probe.
- How well random-projection downsampling works across different model families (llama-like vs mosaic-like). Is there a family-specific tuning?
- Does overlap-chunking play nicely with kv-sharding? Overlap increases duplication across shards; cost model needed.

Actionable next steps (for this sprint):
- (Today) Write a tiny prototype of random-projection downproj as a config flag in local runtime (checkout branch: kv-experiments/downproj-proto). Target: end-of-day smoke tests. -> Assigned: Octavia.
- (3 days) Run probe sweep on 4k/16k traces, collect perf + probe quality. -> Assigned: Octavia + Maya.
- (Next week) Implement fingerprint prototype and run on anonymized 1-hour session trace. If hit-rate > 10% without quality regressions, escalate to a canary test on a low-traffic tenant. -> Assigned: Ravi.

Short bank of heuristics (for later extraction into Optimize):
- if session.take_rate > 0.8 and avg-turn-length > 120 tokens -> enable downproj alpha=0.6 by default; monitor quality.
- if fingerprint.hit_rate > 0.15 -> consider fingerprint-based cache as ephemeral policy for that tenant class.
- if overlap-chunk overhead (memory) < 1.2x -> enable for streaming routes with per-token SLO tighter than 120ms.

Random notes / brain dump:
- Might be useful to pair prefix-fingerprinting with low-dim topic vectors (L2 threshold) rather than raw token hashes. Topic vector sketch could be computed cheaply with a 1-layer projection on the last 64 tokens.
- For the downprojection experiment: test both structured (SVD-ish) and unstructured (random) projections; the structured one may be slower but more stable.
- Keep the probe set public in the repo (small JSON) so reviewers can quickly rerun.

Questions for Maya & Ravi (please reply inline):
- Maya: do we have a canonical anonymized session trace I can use? If not, can you request one from SRE?
- Ravi: any objections to a short canary if prototype looks good? Which tenant class should we pick (low-request-rate staging vs small paid tenant)?

Bottom line: lots of low-cost knobs that could materially reduce token-costs for long sessions. Main friction is careful eval + operational telemetry. I think prototypes will quickly surface what is worth scaling.

summary: Personal reading-scratch: prioritized cheap experiments for KV downprojection, overlap-chunk kernels, and prefix fingerprint cache. Small probe-driven evaluation plan and integration notes. Action items assigned to Octavia, Maya, Ravi.
